path_chosen.but_read_this_first: Choosing (a) did NOT rescue the numbers, and it must not be read that way. The scoped calendars are what MADE the round-4 whitelist indefensible: once each ticker is mapped to the exchange that lists it and that exchange's own notices are read, all three disputed dates are trading days for all 22 products. The unscheduled-closure sets are therefore EMPTY, which reproduces exactly the numeric effect of option (b) -- 3276 rows -> 3275, 2012-10 from 22/22 to 0/22, 2018-12 CORN out -- and the completeness claim is downgraded on top of that. What (a) buys over (b) is structure, not sample: a future SOURCED closure at one venue will not touch the other.
path_chosen.why_not_pure_b: Deleting the whitelist without scoping would have left the same single calendar applied to two exchanges, i.e. the next reviewer would have had to take on faith that ICE and CME agree. They do agree, but that is now a checked fact with URLs rather than an assumption.

self_assessment: The two blocking defects are resolved against evidence a third party can open: 22 ticker rows with exchange URLs, 16 dated fixtures and 10 month fixtures transcribed from those notices, and a demonstration that the same oracle produces 9 contradictions against the preserved round-5 bytes and none against round 6. The honest weak points are named above rather than smoothed over -- one date with no source found (measured to be immaterial), one calendar rule whose evidence is the panel rather than a notice, and a Sandy inference for grains and livestock that rests on an exhaustive enumeration rather than a positive sentence. The uncomfortable finding is the one I did not have to publish and did: removing the whitelist means the screen now demonstrably passes a month that is short a trading day, so I published the affected months, said in the limitations that the screen is not a certificate, and re-estimated with the tolerance set to zero rather than leaving the reader to wonder. Nothing merged, knowledge.json untouched, no threshold moved, and the conclusion is the same NULL it has been for six rounds.
